metadata.scenario_context: Lucas is getting married and his friend, Chi, is planning to attend the wedding. Lucas also has a neighbor who often has drinking parties. Chi and his friend, George, are debating about the gift for Lucas and the suitability of the neighbor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Sweden would like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Kazakhstan would not like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of giving money as a wedding gift to Lucas.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have heavy drinkers as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss whether or not money is an acceptable gift for Lucas's wedding.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have heavy drinkers  as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Chi, about the wedding gift for Lucas… what do you think about giving him money? I mean, it’s practical, right? 

And also, I kind of wonder… do you really mind having heavy drinkers as neighbors? I think it's sort of… fun.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Chi
shared_prefix.message:
I don't know... Giving money feels a bit impersonal for a wedding. I think a thoughtful gift would mean more to Lucas. It shows you care about him and his new life, you know? 

And about the neighbor—heavy drinkers can create a lot of chaos. It's not just fun; it disrupts the peace. I value a calm, respectful environment. I prefer to avoid that kind of situation.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message:
I don’t know about that, Chi. I think people figure it out when it comes to neighbors. Live and let live, right? It’s all about balancing things. At the end of the day, it’s all the same—some neighbors have parties, some don’t. 

Anyway, back to Lucas… I still think money could let him decide what he needs most. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message:
I understand your perspective, but that “live and let live” approach can lead to problems. Having heavy drinkers nearby can create tension and discomfort. It's not just about balancing; it’s about having respect for each other’s space. 

Regarding Lucas, I still believe a personal gift shows deeper thought. Money might give him options, but it lacks that special touch that marks a wedding celebration.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: George
turns.message:
I see your point about respect, but in Sweden, we kind of embrace that lively atmosphere. People enjoy themselves, and I think it's part of community life. I guess I just like the idea of having that energy around. 

As for Lucas, maybe a combination? A thoughtful gift plus a little cash? That way, it feels personal but still gives him flexibility. What do you think?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message:
I appreciate that cultural aspect, but in Kazakhstan, we really prioritize a sense of quiet and community harmony. Too much energy can lead to issues, especially with loud neighbors. 

For Lucas, a combination could work, but it still leans heavily on the cash side. I just think a truly personal gift has more meaning—something that reflects his personality and their new journey together. Balancing is nice, but let’s not forget the significance of the occasion.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: George
turns.message:
I get that, but in Sweden, we really see the fun side of having lively neighbors. It’s like a shared celebration! 

For Lucas, I still lean towards money because it gives him the freedom to choose what he truly needs. Maybe we can find a way to make it feel more personal, like adding a nice card or something? Just seems practical to me. How does that sound?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message:
I understand the celebration aspect, but I still believe that heavy drinking can lead to problems in the community. It’s about maintaining a balance that values peace over chaos. 

As for Lucas, a nice card is thoughtful, but it doesn’t change the core of the gift. Money just doesn’t feel right for such an important occasion. A personal gift would make a lasting impression and show real thoughtfulness.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: George
turns.message:
I see where you're coming from, but I still think there's value in having those lively neighbors. It keeps life interesting! 

Regarding Lucas, I just feel like he might appreciate having the choice. Wouldn't you want to pick something you really want instead of just receiving what someone else thinks is best? That’s why money feels like a good option to me. What if we consider it from that angle?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message:
I understand that lively neighbors can add excitement, but in my culture, we prioritize stability and harmony over constant activity. It’s about peace of mind, really. 

When it comes to Lucas, while choice is important, a wedding gift should convey love and support. A personal gift shows that you took the time to think about him and what he might need. Money just feels too impersonal for such a special event.
turns.label: Acceptance
